hints: After reversing, the first letter and the last letter have traded places. What about the second and the second-last?
Use two pointers, one at each end, and swap the characters they point to while moving inward.

1. Set i = 0, j = n-1.
  2. While i < j, swap letters[i] and letters[j].
  3. Move i right and j left.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: Copy the characters backwards into a new array, then copy them back.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: Swap pairs from both ends moving inward, in place.

explain: For ["d","r","a","w","e","r"]: swap d↔r, r↔e, a↔w, and the pointers meet, giving reward. Each swap puts two characters in their final spots, so only n/2 swaps are needed. With an odd length, the middle character stays where it is; with one character, the loop does nothing.
recognize: Reverse or mirror in place with O(1) memory → two pointers from both ends swapping.
